TheDeclineof the Byzantine Empire
According to historians, no single event brought the Byzantine Empire to an end. Natural
disasters and powerful enemies such as the Arabs, Seljuk Turks, and Ottoman Turks all
contributed to the empire's demise. Most importantly, the Byzantine Empire's incessant
civil wars destroyed a highly efficient military system, a sizable population, trade
network, and economy. While the empire was declining, civil wars hastened its demise.
With the fall of Constantinople, the Russian Empire became the centre of Eastern
European society and Orthodox Christianity.
